title: Poetry-managed virtual environments do not use symlinks on Unix platforms.
body:

- [x] I am on the [latest](https://github.com/sdispater/poetry/releases/latest) Poetry version.

- **OS version and name**: Ubuntu 16.04
- **Poetry version**: latest (master)
- **Link of a [Gist](https://gist.github.com/) with the contents of your pyproject.toml file**: N/A

## Issue

When poetry creates a virtual environment, it does not use symlinks on Unix platforms. Symlinks are the default on Unix platforms when creating a virtual environment with `python -m venv` as seen [here](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/31ec52a9afedd77e36a3ddc31c4c45664b8ac410/Lib/venv/__init__.py#L368). Using symlinks instead of making a copy of the interpreter has several benefits:

1. Less disk usage (I see 28MB used for python and python3 for a virtual environment for Python 3.7.1)
2. Allows usage of `$ORIGIN` in RPATH/RUNPATH in the `python` executable which is useful for relocatable Python builds
3. Easier automatic loading of `python-gdb.py` for gdb debugging helpers
